title: Corollary
body_md: Suppose conditions \eqref{cond_D} and \eqref{cond_L1} are true. Suppose $T$ constructed in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pi_s_k_single_valued} is surjective and $T_*P$ is Ahlfors regular of dimension $d$. Let $r\geq 1$. label: generalized_proof_dai08
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{generalized_proof_dai08}
    In \cite{dai2008quantization}, the author established the proof of $\dim_H^*({P})\leq \underline{\dim}_Q^{r}{(P)}$ when $P$ is supported in $\bigtimes\limits_{i=1}^D [0,1]$. This proof can be further extended to scenarios where the quantizers are constrained within the support , say $\dim_H^*({P})\leq \underline{\dim}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}$, provided that $P$ is compactly supported. The proof can also be generalized to the cases where the quantizers are constrained in the support $K=\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}$, for $P$ compactly supported. In addition \cite[Section 11.3]{graf}, the author proposed the proof for $\underline{\dim}_B(K)=\underline{\dim}_Q^{\infty}{(P)}$ where $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}=K\Subset\mathbb R^D$ under the assumption of unconstrained quantization. This result can also be generalized to the case of constrained quantization when the constraint set itself is $K$, as the proof does not rely on the specific geometry of the quantizers.

label: lemma:monotone_e_n_infty_e_n_r_constrained_10.1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the first argument, using the Jensen's inequality:
    \begin{align*}
        e_{n,r}(P;S)&=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^rdP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r}}=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{s\cdot\frac{r}{s}}dP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{s}\cdot\frac{s}{r}}\\ 
        &\leq \inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^sdP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{s}}=e_{n,s}(P;S)
    \end{align*} If $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}$ is compact, then $\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,0)<\infty$ and therefore $\lim\limits_{r\rightarrow\infty}e_{n,r}(P;S)\leq e_{n,\infty}(P;S)<\infty$. 
    For the second argument, as the mapping $(a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n)\mapsto \{a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n\}$ is $d_H$ continuous for $a_i\in \mathbb R^D$, $\{\alpha\subseteq \mathbb R^D:1\leq|\alpha|\leq n,\alpha\in S\}$ is thus $d_H$ compact. Consider $\alpha_r$ to be the n-optimal set for $e_{n,r}(P;S)$, there exists a subsequence $\{\alpha_{r_k}\}_k$ with the $d_H$ cluster point $\alpha\subseteq S$, then:
    \[\bigg({\int (0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x))^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\leq \sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}|0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x)|=d_H(\alpha_{r_k},\alpha)\]
    with $\alpha_{r_k}\subseteq S$ and $\alpha\subseteq S$. In addition:
    \begin{align*}
    \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}} &\geq \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}-\bigg({\int \bigg|{0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x)}\bigg|^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\\ 
    &\geq \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}-d_H(\alpha_{r_k},S)
    \end{align*}
    from above we can observe 
    \begin{align*}
    \lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}e_{n,r_k}(P;S)&=\lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}\bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\geq \lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}\bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}=\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,\alpha)\\ 
    &\geq \inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,\alpha)=e_{n,\infty}(P;S)
    \end{align*}

label: closedness_pi_inv_s_k
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{closedness_pi_inv_s_k}
    Suppose $\pi_S^{-1}(E)$ is defined in \eqref{eqn:reversal} for $E\in\pi_S(K)$. $\pi_S^{-1}(E)$ is closed if  $E$ is closed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For $F\subseteq \pi_S(K)$ a closed set, let $\{s_n\}_n$ be a converging sequence in $\pi_S^{-1}(F)$ with cluster point $\overline{s}$. Assuming $\overline{s}\not\in \pi_S^{-1}(F)$, which means $\pi_S(\overline{s})\cap F=\varnothing$, by the continuity of the function $f(x)=\inf\limits_{z\in S}0.9355(x,z)$, we have $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}f(s_n)=f(\overline{s})=0.9355(\overline{s},\pi_S(K))$. On the other hand $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}f(s_n)=\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{z\in S}0.9355(s_n,z)=0.9355(\overline{s},F)$. Therefore $0.9355(\overline{s},F)=0.9355(\overline{s},\pi_S(K))$, and thus $\overline{s}\in \pi_S^{-1}(F)$, contradicting $\overline{s}\not\in \pi_S^{-1}(F)$.
head: environment

label: remark:upper_semi_continuity
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark:upper_semi_continuity}
    For a multivalued function $f:X\rightarrow 2^Y$, where $f(x)$ is a set for $x\in X$, we say that $f$ is upper semi-continuous if for any closed set $G\subseteq S$, the set $\{y\in X: f(y)\subseteq G, f(y)\neq\varnothing\}$ is closed, by Kuratowski's definition in \cite{kuratowski2014topology}, and therefore $\pi_S:K\rightarrow 2^S$ is upper semi-continuous.
head: environment

label: compactness_pi_s_k
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{compactness_pi_s_k}
    Suppose $S$ is a closed set and $K=\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}$ is a compact set for a probability measure $P$. $\pi_S(K)$ and $\pi_S^{-1}(E)$ is defined in \eqref{eqn:projection} and \eqref{eqn:reversal} for $E\subseteq \pi_S(K)$. Then $\pi_S(K)$ is compact.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: As the function $f(x)=\inf\limits_{z\in S}0.9355(x,z)$ is continuous and uniformly continuous on $K$, let $g=f|_K$, $g(K)$ is compact $\mathbb R^{+}\cup\{0\}$ and $g(K)=\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^N F_i$ where $F_i$ is closed. Denote $G_i=g^{-1}(F_i)$ and we have $\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^N G_i=K$, as $g^{-1}(g(K))=K$ by the fact that $g=f|_K$. $\pi_S(G_i)$ is bounded and closed, therefore $\pi_S(K)=\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^N \pi_S(G_i)$ is compact.
head: environment

label: lemma:closed_graph_property
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:closed_graph_property}
    For $S\in\mathbb R^D$ a closed set, and $K\Subset\mathbb R^D$ a compact set. The graph of the projection $\pi_S$, denoted, 
    \[\mathrm{{Gr } }\pi_S:\{(x,y)\in K\times S\}:0.9355(x,y)=0.9355(x,S)\},\]
    is compact.
head: environment
name: Closed graph property of $\pi_S(K)$

title: Proof
body_md: Let $f(x,y)=0.9355(x,y)-0.9355(x,S)$, then $f:K\times S\rightarrow\mathbb R$ is continuous. We can rewrite $\text{Gr}\pi_S$ as $\text{Gr}\pi_S=f^{-1}(\{0\})\cap (K\times S)$, therefore $\text{Gr}\pi_S$ is closed. For $(x,y)\in\text{Gr}\pi_S$, we can show that $0.9355(y,0)$ is bounded, and therefore $\text{Gr}\pi_S$ is compact as a closed subset of the product of two compact sets.
head: environment

label: lemma:pi_s_k_single_valued
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:pi_s_k_single_valued}
    For a compact set $K$, if $K=\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}$ for some Borel measure $P$, there exists a single-valued map $T:K\rightarrow \pi_S(K)$, where $T(x)\in \pi_S(x)$, such that $T$ is measurable with respect to $P$.
head: environment
name: Meaurable selector

title: Proof
body_md: In Lemma~\ref{lemma:closed_graph_property}, we showed $\mathrm{Gr}\pi_S$ is compact. In addition, $\pi_S(x)$ is closed. Then we can use the Kuratwoski-Ryll-Nardzewski theorem in \cite{jureczko2023remarks} and \cite[Page 189]{srivastava2008course} to guarantee the existence of a measuable selector.
head: environment

label: lemma:nowhere_dense_pi_s_k
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:nowhere_dense_pi_s_k}
    Suppose $S\cap K=\varnothing$, $S$ is closed in $\mathbb R^D$ and $K$ is compact in $\mathbb R^D$, then $\pi_S(K)$ is nowhere dense.
head: environment
name: Nowhere density of $\pi_S(K)$

title: Proof
body_md: Suppose $\pi_S(K)$ is not nowhere dense, then $(\overline{\pi_S(K)})^\circ=({\pi_S(K)})^\circ\neq\varnothing$, that is, there exists $y\in\pi_S(K)$ and some $r_0>0$ such that $B(y,r_0)\subseteq \pi_S(K)$. Let $x\in\pi_S^{-1}(y)$, and select $z\in B(y,r_0)$ such that $0.9355(y,z)=r_0/2$. We claim that $0.9355(x,z)\geq 0.9355(x,y)$, because otherwise $x\not\in\pi_S^{-1}(y)$. Thereafter, $0.9355(x,z)\geq 0.9355(x,y)\geq 0.9355(x,z)+0.9355(y,z)=0.9355(x,z)+r_0/2$, there is then a contradiction.
head: environment

label: lemma:approximation_pi_s_x_and_pi_s_x_n
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:approximation_pi_s_x_and_pi_s_x_n}
    Let $\{x_n\}_n\subseteq K$ be a sequence converging to $\overline{x}$, then $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\pi_S(\overline{x}),\pi_S(x_n))=0$.
head: environment
name: Stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume the statement is false; then there exist some $a>0$ and some subsequences $\{x_{n_l}\}_l$ such that $0.9355(\pi_S(\overline{x}),\pi_S(x_{n_l}))>a$. Denote $\{x_{n_l}\}_l$ as $\{x_m\}_m$. For each $m\in\mathbb N^{+}$, if $0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))=0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_n))$, then $\pi_S(\overline{x})\cap \pi_S(x_n)\neq \varnothing$, contradicting $0.9355(\pi_S(\overline{x}),\pi_S(x_{m}))>a$. Therefore $0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))<0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_n))$. 
    By the continuity of the function $f(x)=\inf\limits_{z\in S}0.9355(x,z)$, we know that $\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(x_m,\pi_S(x_m))=\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{y\in S}0.9355(x_m,y)=\inf\limits_{y\in S}0.9355(\overline{x},y)=0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))$, and moreover $\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_m))=0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))$ by the fact that \begin{align*}
        \lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_m))&=\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{y\in\pi_S(x_m)}0.9355(\overline{x},y)\leq \lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{y\in\pi_S(x_m)}\bigg({0.9355(\overline{x},x_m)+0.9355(x_m,y)}\bigg)\\
        &=\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(x_m,\pi_S(x_m))=\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{y\in S}0.9355(x_m,y)\\
        &\leq \lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{y\in S}\bigg({0.9355(\overline{x},y)+0.9355(\overline{x},x_m)}\bigg)=\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_m))
    \end{align*} Assume there exists $\{y_k\}_k\subseteq\bigcup\limits_{n=1}^\infty \pi_S(x_n)$ such that $\lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty} 0.9355(\overline{x},y_k)=0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))$, by the compactness of $\pi_S(K)$ from Lemma~\ref{compactness_pi_s_k}, there exists some subsequence $\{y_{k_l}\}_l\subseteq \{y_k\}_k$ converging to some $\overline{y}\in \pi_S(\overline{x})$, contradicting $0.9355(\pi_S(\overline{x}),\pi_S(x_{m}))>a$. Therefore, there exists some $b>0$ such that $0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))+b<0.9355(\overline{x},y)$ for $y\in \bigg(\bigcup\limits_{z\in \pi_S(\overline{x})}\{t:t=z+s,s\in B(0,a/2)\}\bigg)^c$, and therefore $\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_m))>b+0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))$, contradicting the previous established equality that $\lim\limits_{m\rightarrow\infty}0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(x_m))=0.9355(\overline{x},\pi_S(\overline{x}))$.

label: lemma:support_pushforward_measure
title: Lemma
body_md:
(The support of the push-forward measure $T_*P$)\label{lemma:support_pushforward_measure}
    For $P$ a probability measure compactly supported on $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}=K$, with the mapping $T:K\rightarrow \pi_S(K)$ constructed in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pi_s_k_single_valued}, and assume conditions \eqref{cond_A} or \eqref{cond_B} are true, then for the push-forward measure $T_*P$ we have $\text{\normalfont supp} {(T_*P)}=\overline{T(K)}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to assume condition \eqref{cond_A} to be true. For any $x\in\pi_S(K)$, and for any $\varepsilon>0$, by the definition in \eqref{eqn:reversal} we have 
    \begin{align*}
        T^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S)&=\{y\in K:T(y)\in B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S\}\\
        &\supset \{y\in K:\pi_S(y)\subseteq B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S\}=\pi_S^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S)
    \end{align*}
    and therefore $$T_*P(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S)=P(T^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S))\geq P(\pi_S^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S))>0$$ 
    which implies that $\overline{T(K)}\subseteq \text{\normalfont supp} {(T_*P)}$, and on the other hand, $\text{\normalfont supp} {(T_*P)}\subseteq \overline{T(K)}$ as $T(K)\subseteq\overline{T(K)}$.
head: environment

label: lemma:lower_ahlfors_reg_T_*P
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:lower_ahlfors_reg_T_*P}
    For $S\subseteq\mathbb R^D$ a closed set, $P$ a probability measure supported on $K$ which is a compact set, suppose the condition \eqref{cond_D} is true, then there exists $C>0$ such that for any $x\in \overline{T(K)}$ and for any $r>0$ we have $T_*P(B(x,r)\cap S)\geq Cr^s$ where $s=\dim_H(\overline{T(K)})$.
head: environment
name: Lower Ahlfors regularity of the measure $T_*P$

title: Proof
body_md: In the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:support_pushforward_measure} we established that $T_*P(B(x,\varepsilon))\geq P(\pi_S^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S))$, then trivially the lemma is true by the condition \eqref{cond_D}.

label: lemma:monotone_e_n_infty_e_n_r_constrained
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Monotonicity and limit for $e_{n,r}(P;S)$

title: Proof
body_md:
For the first argument, using the Jensen's inequality:
    \begin{align*}
        e_{n,r}(P;S)&=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^rdP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r}}=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{s\cdot\frac{r}{s}}dP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{s}\cdot\frac{s}{r}}\\ 
        &\leq \inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\bigg(\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^sdP(x)\bigg)^{\frac{1}{s}}=e_{n,s}(P;S)
    \end{align*} If $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}$ is compact, then $\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,0)<\infty$ and therefore $\lim\limits_{r\rightarrow\infty}e_{n,r}(P;S)\leq e_{n,\infty}(P;S)<\infty$. 
    For the second argument, as the mapping $(a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n)\mapsto \{a_1,a_2,\cdots,a_n\}$ is $d_H$ continuous for $a_i\in \mathbb R^D$, $\{\alpha\subseteq \mathbb R^D:1\leq|\alpha|\leq n,\alpha\in S\}$ is thus $d_H$ compact. Consider $\alpha_r$ to be the n-optimal set for $e_{n,r}(P;S)$, there exists a subsequence $\{\alpha_{r_k}\}_k$ with the $d_H$ cluster point $\alpha\subseteq S$, then:
    \[\bigg({\int (0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x))^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\leq \sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}|0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x)|=d_H(\alpha_{r_k},\alpha)\]
    with $\alpha_{r_k}\subseteq S$ and $\alpha\subseteq S$. In addition:
    \begin{align*}
    \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}} &\geq \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}-\bigg({\int \bigg|{0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)-0.9355(\alpha,x)}\bigg|^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\\ 
    &\geq \bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}-d_H(\alpha_{r_k},S)
    \end{align*}
    from above we can observe 
    \begin{align*}
    \lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}e_{n,r_k}(P;S)&=\lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}\bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha_{r_k},x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}\geq \lim\limits_{k\rightarrow\infty}\bigg({\int 0.9355(\alpha,x)^{r_k}dP(x)}\bigg)^{\frac{1}{r_k}}=\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,\alpha)\\ 
    &\geq \inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{x\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}}0.9355(x,\alpha)=e_{n,\infty}(P;S)
    \end{align*}

label: lemma:asymp_e_n_infty_regular_pi_k
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:e_n_infty_and_hausdorff_10.4}, $e_{n,\infty}(K;S)=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}d_H(\alpha,K)$ and $e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)=\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow \infty}\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}d_H(\alpha,K)$. Define a new metric $r(x,y):=0.9355(\pi_S(x),\pi_S(y))$ on $K$, and denote the covering radius under $r$ as $e_{n,\infty}(X;S;r)$, then:
    \[e_{n,\infty}(K;S;r)=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S \\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{x\in K}\inf\limits_{a\in\alpha}0.9355(a,\pi_S(x))=\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S \\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{y\in \pi_S(K)}\inf\limits_{a\in\alpha}0.9355(a,y)=e_{n,\infty}(\pi_S(K))\] then
    \begin{align*}
        e_{n,\infty}(K;S)-e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)&\leq\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\in S\\|\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{x\in K}\inf\limits_{a\in\alpha}\bigg({\inf\limits_{p\in\pi_S(x)}\bigg({0.9355(p,x)+0.9355(a,p)}\bigg)}\bigg)-e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)\\
        &\leq \inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S \\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{x\in K}\inf\limits_{a\in\alpha}\bigg({0.9355(\pi_S(x),x)+0.9355(a,\pi_S(x))}\bigg)-e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)\\
        &\leq \sup\limits_{x\in K}0.9355(\pi_S(x),x)+\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S \\ |\alpha|\leq n}}\sup\limits_{y\in K}\inf\limits_{a\in\alpha}0.9355(a,\pi_S(y))-e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)\\
        &=\sup\limits_{x\in K}\inf\limits_{a\subseteq\pi_S(K)}0.9355(a,x)+e_{n,\infty}(\pi_S(K);S)-e_{\infty,\infty}(K;S)\\
        &\leq d_H(\pi_S(K),K)-\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow \infty}\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}d_H(\alpha,K)+e_{n,\infty}(\pi_S(K);S)\\
        &\leq e_{n,\infty}(\pi_S(K);S) \leq e_{n,\infty}(\pi_S(K);\pi_S(K))
    \end{align*}

\label{lemma:conditional_lower_bound}
    Let $S$ be a closed constraint, $P$ be a compactly supported probability with $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}=K$. Suppose that the condition \eqref{cond_L2} is true. label: example:quantizers_out_pi_s_k
title: Example
body_md:
\label{example:quantizers_out_pi_s_k}
 Consider $S=\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $K=\partial B(0,1)$ in $\mathbb R^2$, then there exist a measurable selector $T:K\rightarrow S, x\mapsto x$, which is exactly the identity map. Let $P=U_{\partial B(0,1)}$ be the uniform distribution on $\partial B(0,1)$. $\pi_S(K)=K$ has dimension of 1 in the sense of Hausdorff, box, and Ahlfors and quantization. We will then find the lower constrained quantization dimension. By Corollary~\ref{corollary:upperbound_prob_compactly_supported} and Proposition~\ref{prop:estimate_upper_lower_constrained_quantization_dim}, $\overline{\widehat{\dim}}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}=\overline{\widetilde{\dim}}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}=1$ for $r\geq 1$. By symmetry the $n$ codepoints form a regular $n$--gon
\[
\alpha_n=\{(\theta_i,0.9355):\theta_i=\tfrac{2\pi i}{n},\; i=0,\dots,n-1\},
\qquad 0\le0.9355\le1 .
\]
For a point $(1,t)$ on the unit circle, 
the nearest center is $(0.9355,0)$ after rotation.
The squared distance is 
\(1+0.9355^{2}-20.9355\cos t .\) Therefore
\[
\hat{e}_{n,2}(P;S)=\frac{n}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi/n}^{\pi/n}1+0.9355^{2}-20.9355\cos t \,dt
        =1+0.9355^{2}-\frac{20.9355 n}{\pi}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{n}\Bigr).
\]

Observe that,
\(
\dfrac{d}{d0.9355} \hat{e}_{n,2}(P;S)=20.9355-\dfrac{2n}{\pi}\sin\bigl(\dfrac{\pi}{n}\bigr),
\)
and setting $\dfrac{d}{d0.9355} \hat{e}_{n,2}(P;S)=0$ gives
\[
  0.9355=\frac{n}{\pi}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{n}\Bigr),
\]
which coincide with the result in \cite{rosenblatt2023uniform}. Notice that $0.9355<1$ for any $n$ as $\sin(\pi/n)<\pi/n$ for $n\geq 2$, thus there exists a sequence of $n-$quantizers which lie strictly inside the unit disc as required. This result also coincide with Lemma~\ref{lemma:approximation} that under conditions \eqref{cond_A} and \eqref{cond_B}, the quantizers will approximate $\pi_S(K)$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:conditional_lower_bound}, $\underline{\widehat{\dim}}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}\geq 1$ and $\underline{\widetilde{\dim}}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}\geq 1$, and therefore $\widehat{\dim}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}=\widetilde{\dim}_Q^{r}{(P;S)}=1$. Our results in Section~\ref{section:conditional_lower_bound} and Section~\ref{section:upper_quantization_dimension_estimate} coincide with the quantization dimension as presented in \cite{rosenblatt2023uniform}.

To be concrete, in Example~\ref{example:cond_a_fails} and Figure \ref{figure:condition_a_fails}, the condition \eqref{cond_L1} does not hold. There exists a sequence of $n-$quantizers lying on $\pi_S(K)$. There are two sides separated by the left (right) branch of $S$. Suppose $S_\delta$ to be collection of points on the side without $K$ in the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of $\pi_S(K)$. Then if $b$ is an element of a $n-$quantizer, we can obtain a perturbed $\tilde{b}\in S_\delta$ with $\tilde{b}\not\in \pi_S(K)$ and satisfying$0.9355(\tilde{b},x)>0.9355(x,\pi_S(x))$ for any $x\in K$.

body_md:
\label{example:uniform_unit_circle}
    Let $P$ be a uniform distribution on $K=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ with $S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2\leq \frac{1}{4}\}$. Then $\pi_S(K)=T(K)=\partial S=\{(x,y)\in \mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=\frac{1}{4}\}$. We can construct $T:K\rightarrow \partial S,(x,y)\mapsto (x/2,y/2)$. $T_*P$ will be the uniform distribution on $\partial S$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ and $x\in\pi_S(K)$ we can verify that $\pi_S^{-1}(B(x,\varepsilon)\cap S)\supseteq B(y,c\varepsilon)\cap K$ for some $c>0$, and therefore conditions \eqref{cond_A} and \eqref{cond_D} hold. The condition \eqref{cond_D} also holds as the uniform distribution on $K$ is lower Ahlfors regular of dimension 1.

body_md: This example was given in \cite{pandey2024constrained}. Let $P$ be the Cantor distribution on the Cantor set $\mathcal{C}$ on $\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2: x\in [0,1],y=0\}$. Let $S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:y=1\}$, then $\pi_S(\mathcal{C})=\{(x,y)\in \mathbb R^2:(x,y-1)\in\mathcal{C}\}$. There exists a surjective map $T:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\pi_S(\mathcal{C}), (x,y)\mapsto (x,y+1)$. Therefore $\dim_H{\pi_S(\mathcal{C})}=\dim_H(T(\mathcal{C}))=\dim_H^*({T_*\mathcal{C}})=\dim_H(\mathcal{C})=\dfrac{\log 2}{\log 3}$.

    Suppose conditions \eqref{cond_A} or \eqref{cond_B} are satisfied and $\text{\normalfont supp} {(P)}=K$ is compactly. Let $\alpha_n\in C_{n,\infty}(K;\pi_S(K))$ be the attained n-optimal set, if there exists a sequence of $\{\alpha_n\}_n$ satisfies $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}d_H(\alpha_n,\pi_S(K))=0$, then $$d_H(\pi_S(K),K)\leq \lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\inf\limits_{\substack{\alpha\subseteq S\\ |\alpha|\leq n}}d_H(\alpha,K)$$

title: Proof
body_md:
For any $x\in K'\cup K$ we have $|0.9355(x,A)-0.9355(x,B)|\leq d_H(A,B)$ for any nonempty sets $A\subseteq K'\cup K$ and $B\subseteq K'\cup K$. Here, $K'$ is compact with $\pi_S(K)\subseteq K'$. $K'$ also satisfies that $\alpha_n\subseteq K'$ for $n\geq N$ for some $N\in\mathbb N^{+}$ as $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}d_H(\alpha_n,\pi_S(K))=0$. Furthermore, for some $y\in K'\cup K$ the equality can be achieved for $A=\alpha_n$ and $B=K$. Therefore,
    \begin{align*}
        d_H(\alpha_n,K)-d_H(\pi_S(K),K)&\geq|0.9355(y,\alpha_n)-0.9355(y,K)|-d_H(\pi_S(K),K)\\ 
        &=|0.9355(y,\alpha_n)-0.9355(y,\pi_S(K))+0.9355(y,\pi_S(K))-0.9355(y,K)|-d_H(\pi_S(K),K)\\ 
        &\geq-|0.9355(y,\alpha_n)-0.9355(y,\pi_S(K))|+|0.9355(y,\pi_S(K))-0.9355(y,K)|-d_H(\pi_S(K),K)\\
        &= -|0.9355(y,\alpha_n)-0.9355(y,\pi_S(K))|\geq-\sup\limits_{x\in K}|0.9355(x,\alpha_n)-0.9355(x,\pi_S(K))|\\
        &=-d_H(\alpha_n,\pi_S(K)) >-\varepsilon
    \end{align*}
    followed by a limiting argument. The second equality above is due to we set $|0.9355(x,\pi_S(K))-0.9355(x,K)|=d_H(\pi_S(K),K)$

label: lemma:auxillary_conditional_lower_bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:auxillary_conditional_lower_bound}
    Let $\mu$ be a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R^D$. Assume that there is some $c>0$ and some $r_0>0$ such that $\mu(B(a,r))\leq cr^D$ for all $a\in\text{\normalfont supp} {(\mu)}$ and all $r\in (0,r_0)$, then there exists some constant $c'$ dependent only to $\mu$ and $D$, such that,
    \[\int_B 0.9355(x,a)d\mu(x)\geq c'\mu(B)^{1+1/D},\]
    for all $a\in\mathbb R^D$ and all $B\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb R^D)$.
